title: Adventure Realms - Review; and My Life in Video Games
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TqAy1jbJ9w8

This one comes in two halves. First, Daniel (@dungeondive) reviews Adventure Realms, Peter Jank's follow-up to Quest for the Lost Pixel, published through The Game Crafter with pixel art by Final Boss Blues. Anyone choosing between the two should know they could hardly be more different. Lost Pixel is a dungeon crawl. Adventure Realms is not an adventure game at all but a cut-throat worker placement and deck builder. Your heroes are triple-use cards: sent out as agents, spent as buying power, or pushed down the dungeon track that awards elemental gems and victory points. Guild power can be knocked back down, and the Thieves' Guild lets rivals steal adventure cards from anyone holding three. That fuelled a whole evening of trash talk over his gold-hoarding quest card. The rulebook is clear, the board is among the best-looking he's seen, and his only complaint about the components is a green gem that looks yellow. He hopes it never gets a solo mode, because the competition is the soul of the game.

The second half is a story-time tour of ten video games that shaped his life, in chronological order. Wizardry and The Bard's Tale on the Apple II. Street Fighter II arcade token wars, which led him to change high schools and start his first band. Tomb Raider as a nightly group event. Then Wild Arms, Guardian Heroes, Symphony of the Night, Rez, Dark Souls and Bloodborne, Ys VIII on a hacked Vita, and Assassin's Creed Odyssey.

----

Daniel credits Street Fighter II with changing his school, his friends and his music. Which game (board or video) changed something real in your life?
